answer: A velvet registry takes one 80-credit bond per identity for one juniper seed batch in its garden plot, filing a batch hash and a plume temperature log. Any auditor recomputes germination: 70 percent in the epoch with a matching log, or the bond burns; a duplicate hash or reused log also burns it. Scarcer varieties make the k-th batch pay 30+20(k-1) in fees above the 80 bond, so 1,000 fakes pay 10,020,000 and lock 80,000. A rented seed farm fails: its log is already tied to the original velvet seal. An honest identity pays 110 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
